papers.title: Intuitive Ethics: How Innately Prepared Intuitions Generate Culturally Variable Virtues
papers.abstract_snippet: First statement of Moral Foundations Theory. Proposes that humans come equipped with innate preparedness to feel flashes of approval or disapproval toward patterns involving suffering, hierarchy, reciprocity, and purity, which generate culturally variable virtues.

papers.title: Liberals and Conservatives Rely on Different Sets of Moral Foundations
papers.authors: Graham, J., Haidt, J., & Nosek, B. A.
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Developed measures for five moral foundations (Harm/care, Fairness/reciprocity, Ingroup/loyalty, Authority/respect, Purity/sanctity). Found liberals rely more on Harm/care and Fairness, while conservatives endorse all five foundations more equally.

papers.title: Mapping the Moral Domain
papers.authors: Graham, J., Nosek, B. A., Haidt, J., Iyer, R., Koleva, S., & Ditto, P. H.
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Created and validated the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ). Confirmatory factor analyses supported a 5-factor structure of moral concerns. Established convergent/discriminant validity showing moral concerns predict personality and social group attitudes.

papers.title: The Righteous Mind: Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion
papers.abstract_snippet: Foundational book presenting MFT in full, arguing moral judgments arise from gut feelings rather than logical reason. Applies MFT to explain political and religious differences: liberals prioritize care/fairness, conservatives use all six foundations.

papers.title: Moral Foundations Theory: The Pragmatic Validity of Moral Pluralism
papers.authors: Graham, J., Haidt, J., Koleva, S., Motyl, M., Iyer, R., Wojcik, S. P., & Ditto, P. H.
papers.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive review of MFT's empirical evidence and pragmatic validity. Summarizes findings on five foundations, their evolutionary origins, cross-cultural variation, and political ideology differences.

papers.title: Moral Foundations Twitter Corpus: A Collection of 35k Tweets Annotated for Moral Sentiment
papers.authors: Hoover, J., Portillo-Wightman, G., Yeh, L., Havaldar, S., Davani, A. M., Lin, Y., Kennedy, B., Atari, M., et al.
papers.abstract_snippet: 35,108 tweets from seven domains hand-annotated by trained annotators for 10 categories of moral sentiment (5 virtue/vice pairs). Provides baseline NLP results. Foundational dataset for computational MFT research.

papers.title: The Moral Foundations Reddit Corpus
papers.authors: Trager, J., Ziabari, A. S., Davani, A. M., Golazazian, P., et al.
papers.abstract_snippet: 16,123 Reddit comments from 12 subreddits annotated for 8 moral sentiment categories. Extends MFT annotation beyond Twitter to longer-form social media text, enabling more diverse moral language detection.

papers.title: The Extended Moral Foundations Dictionary (eMFD): Development and Applications of a Crowd-Sourced Approach to Extracting Moral Intuitions from Text
papers.authors: Hopp, F. R., Fisher, J. T., Cornell, D., Huskey, R., & Weber, R.
papers.abstract_snippet: Crowd-sourced moral foundations dictionary using continuous scoring rather than binary categories. Outperforms existing dictionary approaches in extracting moral content from text across multiple domains.

papers.title: MoralBERT: A Fine-Tuned Language Model for Capturing Moral Values in Social Discussions
papers.abstract_snippet: Fine-tuned BERT variants for moral sentiment classification using domain-adversarial training on multiple MFT-annotated datasets. MoralBERT outperforms lexicon methods, traditional ML, and zero-shot GPT-4 by up to 32% F1.

papers.title: Measuring Moral Rhetoric in Text
papers.abstract_snippet: Uses latent semantic analysis to compute semantic similarity between concepts and MFD keywords. Measures moral loading of concepts on five moral dimensions, enabling automated analysis of moral rhetoric in text corpora.

papers.title: Moral Foundations Vignettes: A Standardized Stimulus Database of Scenarios Based on Moral Foundations Theory
papers.authors: Clifford, S., Iyengar, V., Cabeza, R., & Sinnott-Armstrong, W.
papers.abstract_snippet: 132 standardized vignettes depicting violations of specific moral foundations, controlled for syntactic structure and complexity. Suitable for neuroimaging and now used as LLM evaluation stimuli (MFV-LLM benchmark).

papers.title: Morality Beyond the WEIRD: How the Nomological Network of Morality Varies Across Cultures (MFQ-2)
papers.authors: Atari, M., Haidt, J., Graham, J., Koleva, S., Stevens, S. T., & Dehghani, M.
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Develops MFQ-2, a 36-item revised measure with six foundations (Care, Equality, Proportionality, Loyalty, Authority, Purity). Validated across 25 populations; psychometrically superior to original MFQ with improved cross-cultural validity.

papers.title: A Survey on Moral Foundation Theory and Pre-Trained Language Models: Current Advances and Challenges
papers.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive survey reviewing integration of MFT with pre-trained language models. Covers dictionary-based to deep learning operationalization methods, datasets, and applications for moral classification in text.

papers.title: Moral Foundations of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Abdulhai, M., Serapio-Garcia, G., Crepy, C., Valter, D., Canny, J., & Jaques, N.
papers.abstract_snippet: Uses MFT to probe moral foundations encoded in popular LLMs. Finds LLMs exhibit particular moral biases that vary with prompting context; adversarial prompts can shift moral foundations and affect downstream task behavior.

papers.title: MoralBench: Moral Evaluation of LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Benchmark using Moral Foundations Vignettes (MFVs) to evaluate LLM moral reasoning. Tests both numerical moral ratings and written justifications across MFT dimensions, assessing reasoning quality and consistency.

papers.title: Large Language Models Meet Moral Values: A Comprehensive Assessment of Moral Abilities
papers.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive assessment of LLM moral abilities using MFT framework. Evaluates how well LLMs align with human moral values across diverse ethical scenarios and moral foundations.

papers.title: Classification of Moral Foundations in Microblog Political Discourse
papers.abstract_snippet: Early work on automatic classification of moral foundations in political microblog discourse using NLP methods. Demonstrates feasibility of applying MFT to social media text at scale.

papers.title: Are Large Language Models Moral Hypocrites? A Study Based on Moral Foundations
papers.abstract_snippet: Tests whether LLMs exhibit moral hypocrisy by examining consistency between explicit moral foundation endorsements and behavioral responses to moral scenarios. Finds significant inconsistencies across models.
